criteria.description: States that the task adds a native value-based `RANGE` frame type named `WindowFrame.Range`.
States that `WindowFrame.Range` must be registered as Jackson subtype `"range"`.
States that `FramedOnHeapAggregatable#aggregateAll` must accept `Range`.
States that `WindowFramedAggregateProcessor` must accept `Range`.
States that `WindowFirstProcessor` must accept `Range`.
States that `WindowLastProcessor` must accept `Range`.
States that the SQL validator must accept offset `RANGE` frames.
States that Calcite planning must turn offset `RANGE` frames into native frames.
States that offset `RANGE` support must apply only when the window has exactly one `ORDER BY` key.
States that for a non-null ordering key value `v` and a finite offset `o`, a bound must be `v + o` under `ASC`.
States that for a non-null ordering key value `v` and a finite offset `o`, a bound must be `v - o` under `DESC`.
States that a `Range` frame must be the closed interval between its lower bound and its upper bound.
States that unbounded sides of a `Range` frame must reach the partition edges.
States that unbounded sides of a `Range` frame must include rows whose key is `NULL`.
States that a row whose key is `NULL` must resolve finite bounds to the edges of its contiguous `NULL` run.
States that peer rows with equal keys must receive identical frame bounds.
States that peer rows with equal keys must receive identical output.
States that an empty frame must yield the aggregator's zero-row default.
States that `FIRST_VALUE` must return `null` on an empty frame.
States that `LAST_VALUE` must return `null` on an empty frame.
States that a `Range` covering the whole partition for every row must evaluate the same as `WindowFrame.unbounded()`.
States that range resolution must work for every `RowsAndColumns` implementation.
States that timestamp columns reach the native engine as `LONG`.
States that an ordering type unable to do value arithmetic with a finite offset must throw an unchecked `DruidException`.
States that a day-time `INTERVAL` offset must map to its millisecond magnitude as a floating-point value without integer truncation.
States that the single `ORDER BY` key of an offset `RANGE` frame must be numeric or a timestamp.
States that an offset `RANGE` frame with finite bounds on a non-numeric and non-interval key must be rejected.
States that `Range` must support Jackson serialization.
States that `Range` must support Jackson deserialization.
States that `WindowFrame.Range` must have a `@Nullable Double lowerOffset`.
States that `WindowFrame.Range` must have a `@Nullable Double upperOffset`.
States that `WindowFrame.Range` must have a non-null `ColumnWithDirection orderBy`.
Names `WindowFrame.range` as the required static factory for building a `Range`.
States that `Range` must override `equals` by value.
States that `Range` must override `hashCode` by value.
States that the agent found earlier that only `DefaultFramedOnHeapAggregatable` implements `FramedOnHeapAggregatable`.
States that `WindowFrame.Range` implements `WindowFrame` directly instead of extending `OffsetFrame`.
States that the positive SQL `RANGE` tests omit an outer `ORDER BY` because `testWindowingWithOrderBy` asserts window results without one.
States that `testUnSupportedRangeBoundsOnStringKey` expects a `QueryException` with the code `QueryException.SQL_QUERY_UNSUPPORTED_ERROR_CODE`.
States that the `Range` branch in `isEffectivelyUnbounded` goes before the `OffsetFrame` unwrap because the agent judged the unwrap would fail on a `Range`.
States that `Calcites.isLongType` counts `TIMESTAMP` as a long type.
States that `testUnSupportedRangeBounds` now runs `ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY dim1, dim2 RANGE BETWEEN 3 PRECEDING AND 2 FOLLOWING)`.
States that under `ASC` the frame end is the first row whose value is greater than the upper bound.
States that the positive SQL `RANGE` tests will check only `expectedResults`, not `expectedQuery`.

States that the peer groups come from `computeBoundaries` on the `ORDER BY` column.
States that keys are compared as doubles through `accessor.getDouble(row)`.
States that under `DESC` the frame end is the start of the null run when no non-null row is below the upper bound.
States that under `ASC` the frame starts at the first row whose value is at least the lower bound.
States that under `DESC` the frame starts at the first row whose value is at most the lower bound.
States that the binary search covers only the non-null rows because the agent found earlier that `getDouble` on a null row gives 0.0.
